run.resultText:
I reviewed the plan against the brief, the sketch-derived outcome description, and the eight task specs.

**What's solid:**
- Scope assessment (M, low risk, 2 phases/8 tasks) is honest — greenfield app, no existing system to break, matches the "standard" medium-job process.
- Tooling is set up in the very first task (`p1-setup`), so every subsequent task's verify commands are runnable from the start.
- Test tiering matches the global CLAUDE.md guidance well: per-task verify runs filtered test files (e.g. `npm test -- src/lib/dates.test.ts`), full suite + build only at each phase gate.
- The two important aspects called out in the brief are both addressed concretely: streak/date correctness gets its own hardened module (`dates.ts` never uses `toISOString`/UTC, explicit leap-year/DST test cases) with a `sonnet/high` model assignment reflecting its risk; "ticking feels instant" is handled by an explicit optimistic-update-then-persist pattern in `p1-state` with rollback on failure.
- Tasks are scoped to single sessions with precise, checkable acceptance criteria, and verify commands genuinely exercise those criteria (dedicated test files per task).
- Dependency chain and phase split are sensible; priority-5 "Daily check-in" ships in phase 1, priority-5 "Habits" CRUD follows immediately in phase 2 — reasonable given this is already a minimal 2-phase plan.

**One concrete problem:** the outcome copy oversells what phase 1 builds. "What the owner gets" states the owner can "fix yesterday or any day in the last week," but every task that implements catch-up (`p1-today-screen`'s "YESTERDAY · CATCH UP" block, and its own bullet list two lines below) only covers **yesterday** — there is no task, acceptance criterion, or UI element anywhere in the plan that lets the owner edit a day further back than yesterday (the 7-day `.spark` strip is explicitly read-only display). This is an internal inconsistency between the plan's own summary and its own task specs, not just a minor copy nit — the owner will expect a capability nothing in the 8 tasks delivers.

<<<JSON
{ "decision": "rework", "rationale": "Plan is well-scoped, well-sequenced, and correctly prioritizes the brief's critical date/streak correctness and instant-tick requirements, but the owner-facing outcome text overpromises catch-up functionality that no task actually builds.", "feedback": "Fix the 'What the owner gets' summary: it says the owner can 'fix yesterday or any day in the last week,' but the only catch-up mechanism specified anywhere in the plan (p1-today-screen's 'YESTERDAY · CATCH UP' block, confirmed by its own bullet list below) covers only yesterday — there's no task or acceptance criterion for editing any day further back, and the 7-day spark strip is explicitly read-only. Either (a) change the outcome text to just 'fix yesterday' to match what p1-today-screen actually builds, or (b) if a full week of catch-up is really intended, extend p1-today-screen's spec and acceptance criteria to make the catch-up block (or the spark strip) cover and allow ticking the last 7 days, not just yesterday." }
JSON>>>
